texts.preamble: In Re vs Ram Singh on 29 March, 2016 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 132/04 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0196412004 Date of Institution: 06.07.2004 Date of reserving judgement: 05.03.2016 Date of pronouncement: 29.03.2016 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Ram Singh S/o. Sh. Surat Singh R/o. Rz-20D, Sagapur, New Delhi ... Accused Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules. The acc
texts.facts: The acc used Ram Singh is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Kwality Sweets, from where the food article, that is, 'Rasbhari' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 17.03.2004, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) P. C. Tiwari and Field Assistant (FA) Bhopal Singh under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Dr. Anil Kumar reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Kwality Sweets at WZ-1193, Nangal Rai, New Delhi-46, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Rasbhari from the vendor, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 08.04.2004, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it contained added starch and vegetable oil which were not declared as ingredients. Upon receipt of report, the In Re vs Ram Singh on 29 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77358429/ 1 SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 06.07.2004 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 06.07.2004. The accused appeared and stated on 14.07.2004 that he did not want to exercise his right under section 13(2) of PFA Act for sending the sample for analysis to the Central Food Laboratory. The matter was then listed for pre-charge evidence. 4. The prosecution examined PW-1 FI P. C. Tiwari in pre-charge evidence. On the basis of his testimony, charge was framed against the accused vide order dated 09.03.2009, for commission of offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Upon this, PW-1 was recalled for further cross-examination in post-charge evidence. Additionally, complainant examined FA PW-2 Bhopal Singh and SDM/LHA PW-3 Sh. Anil Aggarwal in post-charge evidence. 5. PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 17.03.2004 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms of Rasbhari, cutting the same into smallest possible pieces using a clean and dry knife, mixing/homogenizing it, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding preservative formalin (40 drops each), fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/D and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received upon which investigation was carried out. Letters Ex. PW-1/G and Ex. PW-1/J were written to STO and MCD. Accused also furnished his reply Ex. PW-1/H. Sanction Ex. PW-1/L was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex. PW-1/M was then filed in the court. Copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/N was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex. PW-1/O. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sample was not adulterated. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 02.05.2013 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 17.03.2004, yet he claimed that no efforts were made to join public witnesses and that the price of sample was not paid to him. He stated that the bottled were not clean and dry and claimed that the vegetable oil and starch detected were from pista pieces present in the sample of Rasbhari. He chose to lead evidence in defence. 7. In defence, the accused examined DW-1 Sh. S. N. Mahendru, a chemical expert. He deposed that pista contains its own starch and vegetable oil and when fats and oils are extracted in a solvent, In Re vs Ram Singh on 29 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77358429/ 2 inherent oil of pista and inherent fat of rasbhari would come in the solvent. During cross-examination by the Ld. SPP for complainant, he opined that without identifying the oil or starch, it would be vague to state that there was added oil or added starch in the sample.
texts.arguments: 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings in the PA report. It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the sample proceedings were not conducted properly and that there are missing links in the case. Ld. Counsel has strongly contended there is no standard prescribed for Rasbhari as a food article and in the absence of prescribed standard, it cannot be said that any Rule has been violated. It is also submitted that the PA report nowhere shows if the starch and oil detected by it were due to added pista pieces or not. 12. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be.
